questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not have many crucial aspects concerning my choice of study destination, but I wanted to go to somewhere where I could further my understanding and relation to architecture and city planning. So choosing a bigger city like Bristol made sense. And now I'm happy that it was close enough to home, so that I can easily come back and visit in the future.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Once I arrived in Bristol, everything ran pretty smoothly. The university had lots of orientation meetings planned for us, and were easy to reach if needed. They kept updating us all through the semester whether it was regarding deadlines, events, opportunities etc. They also hosted continuous events where exchange students could meet up, not only in the first weeks but all the way through. There was always someone available in the "global lounge" if you needed assistance in any way.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed assistance with changing units, which they quickly and without trouble helped me do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Lots of accommodation opportunities were available all across campus, catering to all needs, preferences, and budgets.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I personally chose a non-catered accommodation, so we had a shared kitchen. However there was lots of other accommodation with catering.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: For me, the accommodation was actually the best part of my exchange. I lived in Manor Hall, which was one of my top wishes when applying for accommodation even though I did not know what to expect from it. Originally I was looking for private accommodation, but I decided to apply for campus housing last minute. We were 17 people sharing a hall/kitchen/bath and even though it sounds like a lot, the people I ended up living with became my best friends. The only thing I would let future exchange students now, is that people in Bristol are relatively younger - I was 25 when leaving for my exchange, and everyone I lived with was between 18-20. For me, it was not a problem at all and I did not really recognize the age difference. If it is not for you, I would recommend looking for private accommodation, although I would really recommend not worrying about it and choosing a place like Manor Hall if you have the possibility.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to book a time slot to stop by the senate house (main campus) and show all your registration papers/passport. It was very easy to find and took no more than 10 minutes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university had provided us with an exchange student inbound team, who were always easy to reach via email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The registration at University of Bristol ran smoothly so I would recommend not worrying to much about that part and always just reach out to the inbound-team with any questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not feel that the courses I chose matched the academic level from my studies back home. I wouldn't say it was a problem with the academic programme at your host institution though, but rather that I just chose the wrong courses/units.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: If you want the academic level to match the one back home I would, from my personal experience, recommend choosing higher level courses/units. I chose only open units, as they did not have many requirements and I was concerned with getting my choices approved by KU. I found that the courses, although interesting, did not really match the academic level and were a bit irrelevant for my education.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Even if my choices might have been a bit off, I think that the style of teaching at UOB is really good and made the courses interesting.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sustainable Development, City Futures & Creative Futures

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depending on your degree, I would just really recommend reading all the course descriptions thoroughly. All my courses were open units which I found out meant that people from lots of different degrees took them. I made the units seem a bit random, and a bit off topic from my own degree.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not unexpected, but I also travelled a lot around the UK, to Scotland and Wales etc. This was of course an added expense, but I would totally recommend traveling while you're here.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I did not spend any money on school supplies or books for my courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: University offered all kinds of different sports and societies to join - basically there was a society for every interest imaginable. I would really recommend joining one, it's a great way to meet people! The first week of the semester the societies will host "give it a go's" where you can try them out free of charge.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely joining a society

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to some of the nearby cities, I went to London a lot and loved it, but also Cornwall, Cardiff, Bath etc. Scotland is not far away and an amazing place to visit especially if you're into hiking/nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy for me personally

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My best tip is choosing a student accommodation through the University. The more people the better. Other than that, joining a sport or society is definitely worth it.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the only cultural difference for me was the age of students in Bristol. Unlike home, they mostly go straight from college (gymnasium) to University which means that they're all about 18-20. I had lots of gaps years before starting university back home, so there was obviously quite an age gap between us. However, I did not feel that it caused any trouble in regards to meeting people or making friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: In my opinion, people in the UK are so friendly and polite, which means everyone is easy to talk to. Even just when shopping, going for a walk or talking to people all around Bristol everyone is so kind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Dont be afraid of campus accommodation (choose manor hall if possible)
Explore ALL of the city, especially areas like Stokes Croft, Clifton, Southville, and all the small surrounding areas. (Also wild swimming!)
Use all the green areas and parks as much as possible

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pub nights will be a big expense:)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning a lot about myself, and getting to know the people here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trusting that I know how to meet people and make friends, and learning that everything happens for a reason it will all work out the way it's supposed to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Going on an exchange might seem overwhelming especially in the planning/application process but it is so worth it. It's something I'll cherish and remember for the rest of my life.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
